scenes.tts: Excitatory cortical neurons are born in zones at the bottom of the wall, then climb. So how can you tell, weeks later, when one was born?
scenes.visual: Title card: Dating a Birthday. A mature cortex with one neuron circled. Question: when was it born?
scenes.narration: Excitatory cortical neurons are born in zones at the bottom of the wall, then climb. So how can you tell, weeks later, when one was born?

scenes.tts: You date its last S phase, when DNA is copied. That is the final S phase of the cell that divides to make it.
scenes.visual: A cell-cycle ring with S phase highlighted, then a division making a neuron. Label: birthday = the last S phase before the neuron is made.
scenes.narration: You date its last S phase, when DNA is copied. That is the final S phase of the cell that divides to make it.

scenes.tts: Give a pregnant mouse one dose of thymidine carrying tritium, a radioactive form of hydrogen.
scenes.visual: A pregnant mouse receives one injection. Label: tritiated thymidine, one pulse.
scenes.narration: Give a pregnant mouse one dose of thymidine carrying tritium, a radioactive form of hydrogen.

scenes.tts: Only DNA uses thymidine. So only cells copying DNA in the next hour or so are marked.
scenes.visual: Dividing cells in the ventricular zone; only those in S phase light up with black grains on their nuclei.
scenes.narration: Only DNA uses thymidine. So only cells copying DNA in the next hour or so are marked.

scenes.tts: The labeled cell still divides once to make a neuron. Each extra division after that halves the label.
scenes.visual: A labeled S-phase cell divides once; its daughter leaves the cycle, fully labeled. Dilution table builds row by row: extra divisions before leaving 0, full; 1, half; 2, a quarter; 3, an eighth. Grain counts on nuclei shrink to match. Label: idealized.
scenes.narration: The labeled cell still divides once to make a neuron. Each extra division after that halves the label.

scenes.tts: A neuron still heavily labeled weeks later made its last DNA copy while the label was there. The pulse dates its birth.
scenes.visual: The full-label row highlighted; a heavily labeled neuron with label: left the cycle at the first division after the pulse. Small note: marks a cohort born around the pulse.
scenes.narration: A neuron still heavily labeled weeks later made its last DNA copy while the label was there. The pulse dates its birth.

scenes.tts: The label marks that S phase. It does not tell the cell anything.
scenes.visual: The grains drawn as a date stamp, not an arrow. Label: a record, not an instruction.
scenes.narration: The label marks that S phase. It does not tell the cell anything.

scenes.tts: Now two models. In model one, each new neuron is added at the bottom and shoves the older ones outward.
scenes.visual: Left column, Model 1: push. New neurons appear at the base, beneath the older ones; older ones are shoved upward.
scenes.narration: Now two models. In model one, each new neuron is added at the bottom and shoves the older ones outward.

scenes.tts: In model two, each new neuron climbs past the older ones and settles above them.
scenes.visual: Right column, Model 2: pass. New neurons climb past older ones and settle above.
scenes.narration: In model two, each new neuron climbs past the older ones and settles above them.

scenes.tts: Predict. Pulse on embryonic day twelve, then look at postnatal day twenty-one. Where does each model put the heavily labeled cells?
scenes.caption: Predict. Pulse on embryonic day 12 (E12), then look at postnatal day 21 (P21). Where does each model put the heavily labeled cells?
scenes.visual: Predict card between the two columns: E12 pulse, look at P21. Where are the labeled cells in each model?
scenes.narration: Predict. Pulse on embryonic day 12 (E12), then look at postnatal day 21 (P21). Where does each model put the heavily labeled cells?

scenes.tts: Model one puts them nearest the surface, shoved up by everything added beneath them. Model two puts them deepest.
scenes.visual: Model 1 column: labeled cells at the top. Model 2 column: labeled cells at the bottom.
scenes.narration: Model one puts them nearest the surface, shoved up by everything added beneath them. Model two puts them deepest.

scenes.tts: In nineteen sixty-one, Jay Angevine and Richard Sidman gave pulses on different embryonic days.
scenes.caption: In 1961, Jay Angevine and Richard Sidman gave pulses on different embryonic days.
scenes.visual: Credit: Angevine and Sidman, 1961, mouse. A row of pulse days along a timeline.
scenes.narration: In 1961, Jay Angevine and Richard Sidman gave pulses on different embryonic days.

scenes.tts: Cells labeled earliest lay deepest, beside the white matter. Cells labeled later lay progressively nearer the surface.
scenes.visual: Real-data panel: early cohorts deep beside the white matter, later cohorts nearer the surface. Model 2 column gets a check mark.
scenes.narration: Cells labeled earliest lay deepest, beside the white matter. Cells labeled later lay progressively nearer the surface.

scenes.tts: Later cells had passed earlier ones. It is a strong tendency, with overlap between days.
scenes.visual: Overlapping cohort bands, colour by pulse day. Label: strong tendency, overlap between days.
scenes.narration: Later cells had passed earlier ones. It is a strong tendency, with overlap between days.

scenes.tts: Here is the signature evidence, idealized. Heavily labeled cells from an embryonic day twelve pulse sit mostly in layers five and six.
scenes.caption: Here is the signature evidence, idealized. Heavily labeled cells from an E12 pulse sit mostly in layers 5 and 6.
scenes.visual: Idealized table/bar chart by layer, surface at top: E12 column shows most heavy label in layer 6 and subplate, many in layer 5, few above.
scenes.narration: Here is the signature evidence, idealized. Heavily labeled cells from an E12 pulse sit mostly in layers 5 and 6.

scenes.tts: From an embryonic day sixteen pulse, they sit mostly in layers two and three.
scenes.caption: From an E16 pulse, they sit mostly in layers 2 and 3.
scenes.visual: E16 column added: most heavy label in layers 2 and 3, few below. Label: idealized.
scenes.narration: From an E16 pulse, they sit mostly in layers 2 and 3.

scenes.tts: Lightly labeled cells divided again after the pulse. Born later, at many times, they scatter through many layers.
scenes.visual: Faint grey dots scattered across all layers. Label: lightly labeled, born after the pulse.
scenes.narration: Lightly labeled cells divided again after the pulse. Born later, at many times, they scatter through many layers.

scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy-four, Pasko Rakich found the same order in the visual cortex of rhesus monkeys.
scenes.caption: In 1974, Pasko Rakic found the same order in the visual cortex of rhesus monkeys.
scenes.visual: Credit: Rakic, 1974, rhesus monkey visual cortex. The same inside-out bands beside a monkey brain outline.
scenes.narration: In 1974, Pasko Rakic found the same order in the visual cortex of rhesus monkeys.

scenes.tts: In the mouse, layers two to six are made over about six embryonic days. Subplate and layer six come first, upper layers last.
scenes.caption: In the mouse, layers 2 to 6 are made over about six embryonic days. Subplate and layer 6 come first, upper layers last.
scenes.visual: Timeline E11 to E17 under the column, colour bands for subplate and layer 6 first, upper layers last. Label: mouse numbers; classes overlap.
scenes.narration: In the mouse, layers 2 to 6 are made over about six embryonic days. Subplate and layer 6 come first, upper layers last.

scenes.tts: Then each later wave passes the neurons already in the cortical plate and settles above them.
scenes.visual: Step 3: a gold neuron climbs past older cortical-plate neurons. Layer 6 lit first, layer 2 last.
scenes.narration: Then each later wave passes the neurons already in the cortical plate and settles above them.

scenes.tts: Notice the exception. The preplate cells are born first, yet they end up both at the top and at the bottom. Earlier means deeper only inside the cortical plate.
scenes.visual: Preplate cells highlighted in both the marginal zone (top) and the subplate (bottom).
scenes.narration: Notice the exception. The preplate cells are born first, yet they end up both at the top and at the bottom. Earlier means deeper only inside the cortical plate.

scenes.tts: This is a rule of the neocortex. The retina uses birth order too, but builds its layers another way.
scenes.visual: Small retina panel beside the cortex. Label: birth order biases cell type; layers not built by passing.
scenes.narration: This is a rule of the neocortex. The retina uses birth order too, but builds its layers another way.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: a thymidine pulse dates a birthday, and later-born neurons pass earlier ones to settle above them.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card over the inside-out column with the dilution table in the corner.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: a thymidine pulse dates a birthday, and later-born neurons pass earlier ones to settle above them.
